directive_text_verbatim:
# CODER — NEXT MOVE

**Read Constitution v2.1.0 completely before coding. Read it completely again before the final commit.**

Do **not** install Blender, OpenFOAM, SOFA, Chrono, or another solver yet.

### Phase 1 — Build `PHYSICS_COVERAGE_REGISTRY_V1`

Create a machine-readable registry containing, for every supported physical phenomenon:

```text
phenomenon
governing_equations
solver
solver_version
geometry_requirements
boundary_conditions
material_requirements
operating_regime
validated_regime
known_limitations
uncertainty
verification_method
epistemic_class
input_schema
output_schema
```

Start with the existing hydraulic solver.

### Phase 2 — Build the coverage matrix

Take the currently dead R411/R412 mechanisms and classify them deterministically:

```text
hydraulic
structural
thermal
electromagnetic
acoustic
multibody
soft-body
chemical
optical
multiphysics
UNKNOWN
```

Generate:

**candidate count by physics domain**

**percentage currently simulatable**

**percentage currently terminating as `MECHANISM_NOT_SIMULATABLE`**

**expected candidates unlocked by each missing domain**

This determines which solver gets built next.

### Phase 3 — Deterministic solver routing

Do **not** allow an LLM to be the sole solver selector.

Create a deterministic rule/ontology layer:

```text
mechanism terminology
→ physical phenomena
→ required equations
→ eligible solver domains
→ registry lookup
```

An LLM may propose a classification, but the registry/rules must verify it.

### Phase 4 — Establish the geometry boundary

Write this into the architecture and tests:

> **CadQuery is the engineering geometry authority; Blender is a downstream visualization/rendering system and cannot originate or independently validate engineering geometry.**

Then test that boundary.

### Phase 5 — Choose exactly ONE new solver

Use the coverage matrix.

Do not choose it because it is fashionable.

Choose the domain with the highest:

```text
candidate unlock
×
expected information gain
÷
integration cost
```

Only then select the external solver.

### Phase 6 — Fully wire that solver

The standard is not:

> "Solver installed."

The standard is:

```text
mechanism
→ geometry
→ solver
→ simulation
→ result
→ evidence artifact
→ verification
→ attacker
→ dossier
```

At least one real candidate must traverse that complete path.

### Phase 7 — Only then integrate Blender

Once the physical solver produces a verified result:

```text
verified geometry
+
verified simulation output
↓
Blender
↓
web GLB
PDF render
exploded view
section view
simulation visualization
```

The render should reference the **simulation artifact ID**, so the PDF/website can never imply that Blender itself established the physical result.

# One major improvement I want beyond the auditor

Add a **Physics Gap Opportunity Score**.

For every missing solver domain:

```text
dead candidates unlocked
mechanism diversity
expected information gain
implementation cost
validation maturity
automation feasibility
```

Then the machine itself tells us:

> "Structural mechanics would unlock 31 candidates at estimated integration cost X, while electromagnetics would unlock 4."

That turns physics expansion into a **measured discovery investment decision**, rather than architecture-by-opinion.

# Current checklist

| Area                                      | Status                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Physics Coverage Registry                 | 🔴 Not built                                      |
| Physics coverage measurement              | 🔴 Not built                                      |
| Deterministic solver routing              | 🔴 Not built                                      |
| Existing hydraulic solver                 | 🟢 Operational                                    |
| Second solver                             | 🔴 Not yet selected                               |
| Geometry authority boundary               | 🟡 Needs formalization                            |
| CadQuery                                  | 🟡 Existing but environment issue remains         |
| Blender                                   | 🔴 Do not integrate yet                           |
| Physics → evidence artifacts              | 🟡 Partial                                        |
| Physics → attacker                        | 🟡 Existing architecture, broader domains missing |
| Physics → buyer dossier                   | 🟡 Partial                                        |
| Multi-physics                             | 🔴 Not yet                                        |
| End-to-end computational engineering loop | 🔴 Not yet proven                                 |

The key principle is:

> **Do not build a bigger physics stack. Build a physics decision machine that earns each new solver by demonstrated discovery value.**

That keeps the system aligned with the actual objective: **discovering and producing credible inventions**, not accumulating scientific software.
